The strongest argument for deregulation derives from what might be called free speech absolutism—the position that government has no legitimate authority to restrict expression based on its content, however offensive, disturbing, or valueless that content may appear to majorities or authorities.

This principle finds its philosophical foundations in John Stuart Mill's On Liberty, which argues that society lacks authority to silence any opinion because we can never be certain of its falsity, because even false opinions contain partial truths, and because unchallenged truths become "dead dogma." The deregulatory alternative—removing government from sexual expression evaluation entirely—avoids these institutional pathologies while preserving the consent-based protections that prevent genuine harm.
